source.body:
# Open Grant Proposal: `FileVect: Decentralized Vector Embedding Search & Indexing Engine for FVM`

**Project Name:** `FileVect`

**Proposal Category:** `Developer and data tooling`

**Individual or Entity Name:** Entity on behalf of Kovach Enterprises LLC

**Proposer:** `igor-holt`

**Project Repo(s):** `[https://github.com/igor-holt/filevect](https://github.com/igor-holt/filevect)`

**(Optional) Filecoin ecosystem affiliations:** `Kovach Enterprises LLC maintains active development pipelines within decentralized data infrastructure and Protocol Labs Network interoperability frameworks.`

**(Optional) Technical Sponsor:** `None`

**Do you agree to open source all work you do on behalf of this RFP under the MIT/Apache-2 dual-license?:** `Yes`

# Project Summary

The rapid expansion of decentralized artificial intelligence and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems has created an immense demand for high-performance, verifiable vector embedding databases. However, storing and querying high-dimensional vector spaces in a fully trustless, decentralized manner remains a major bottleneck. Current AI infrastructure heavily relies on centralized vector databases (such as Pinecone or Milvus) or ephemeral local indices, introducing single points of failure, censorship risks, and a complete lack of cryptographic verifiability for similarity searches.

`FileVect` is an open-source, decentralized vector embedding search and indexing engine natively integrated with the Filecoin Virtual Machine (FVM) and InterPlanetary File System (IPFS). By combining Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph indices with content-addressed decentralized storage, `FileVect` enables developers to store, index, and perform low-latency approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) vector searches over datasets stored immutably on Filecoin. Smart contracts executing on the FVM can securely trigger verifiable similarity queries, allowing decentralized AI agents, autonomous market makers, and semantic search protocols to query massive datasets without trusting a centralized intermediary.

This project will deliver a production-ready Rust-based vector indexing crate optimized for FVM smart contracts, a decentralized query routing protocol, and comprehensive developer tooling including TypeScript SDKs and sample dApps. By bridging high-performance vector retrieval with Filecoin's robust storage guarantees, `FileVect` unlocks a new paradigm of verifiable, data-rich decentralized intelligence.

## Impact

`FileVect` addresses a critical infrastructure gap in the Web3 and decentralized AI ecosystems: the inability to perform scalable, trustless semantic searches over large-scale unstructured datasets stored on Filecoin. As developers increasingly build on-chain machine learning models, autonomous agents, and decentralized knowledge graphs, they are forced to compromise by offloading vector search to centralized cloud providers. This creates severe security vulnerabilities, data lock-in, and compliance risks.

The primary pain point solved by `FileVect` is the friction between immutable, cold storage (Filecoin) and hot, high-frequency vector retrieval requirements. Getting this right will establish Filecoin as the premier settlement and retrieval layer for the emerging decentralized AI stack, driving substantial data onboarding and transaction volume on the FVM. Conversely, failing to provide native vector tooling risks alienating the next generation of AI developers who require high-performance similarity search as a core primitive.

The impact of this project spans across the decentralized AI, decentralized storage, and Web3 data tooling verticals. Success will be measured by developer adoption (number of unique repositories integrating the SDK), query throughput benchmarks under FVM gas constraints, and the total volume of vector-indexed data successfully onboarded and pinned to the Filecoin network.

## Outcomes

The final deliverables for `FileVect` will include:

1. **Core Rust Vector Engine (`filevect-core`):** A high-performance HNSW vector indexing and quantization library optimized for WebAssembly (Wasm) execution and FVM compatibility.
2. **FVM Smart Contract Bindings:** Solidity and Rust smart contract interfaces enabling FVM actors to initiate, verify, and settle decentralized vector search queries and proof-of-retrieval validations.
3. **Decentralized Gateway Node (`filevect-node`):** An open-source routing node service that indexes content-addressed chunks from IPFS/Filecoin and serves high-speed ANN queries over gRPC and JSON-RPC.
4. **Developer SDK & Documentation:** A comprehensive TypeScript SDK (`@filevect/sdk`), CLI tooling, and a fully documented end-to-end example dApp demonstrating decentralized RAG.

**Success Metrics:**

* **Performance:** Sub-50ms query latency for top-k nearest neighbor searches over 1 million 1536-dimensional vectors.
* **Gas Efficiency:** FVM gas consumption optimized to execute verification proofs within standard block gas limits.
* **Ecosystem Adoption:** At least 5 external developer teams building testnet prototypes using `FileVect` within 3 months of mainnet release.

## Data Onboarding

* Month #1: `1 TB`
* Month #3: `10 TB`
* Month #6: `50 TB`
* Month #12: `250 TB`

## Adoption, Reach, and Growth Strategies

The target audience for `FileVect` consists of Web3 AI developers, decentralized data DAO contributors, autonomous agent engineers, and traditional data infrastructure teams seeking trustless alternatives to cloud vector databases. We plan to engage this audience through targeted developer workshops, hackathon sponsorships within the Filecoin and broader Ethereum/FVM developer communities, and technical deep-dives published on Mirror and GitHub.

To onboard our first 10 users, we will directly reach out to existing Filecoin storage clients, FVM grant recipients, and AI hackathon participants, offering hands-on engineering support and custom integration guides. To scale to our first 100 users, we will launch public incentivized testnet bounties, comprehensive documentation, and pre-built templates for popular AI frameworks (such as LangChain and LlamaIndex) to ensure seamless drop-in replacement of centralized vector stores.

## Development Roadmap

### Milestone 1: Core Rust Engine & Indexing Specifications

* **Functionality:** Implementation of the core HNSW graph construction, vector quantization (scalar and product quantization), and in-memory similarity metrics (Cosine, Euclidean, Dot Product) in Rust, compiled successfully to Wasm.
* **Team Size & Roles:** 2 Engineers (Igor Holt as Lead Systems Architect; Andrew Kovach overseeing core integration logic).
* **Funding Required:** `$12,000`
* **Completion Date:** `May 31, 2026`

### Milestone 2: FVM Smart Contract Integration & Verification

* **Functionality:** Development of FVM smart contract bindings in Rust/Solidity, enabling decentralized query dispatch, result commitment verification, and cryptographic proof-of-retrieval validation.
* **Team Size & Roles:** 2 Engineers (Igor Holt as Lead Smart Contract Engineer; Andrew Kovach handling deployment automation).
* **Funding Required:** `$15,000`
* **Completion Date:** `July 15, 2026`

### Milestone 3: Decentralized Gateway Node & TypeScript SDK

* **Functionality:** Creation of the `filevect-node` routing service for indexing Filecoin/IPFS data chunks, alongside a robust TypeScript SDK (`@filevect/sdk`) and CLI for developer interaction.
* **Team Size & Roles:** 2 Engineers (Igor Holt managing gateway architecture; Andrew Kovach managing SDK distribution).
* **Funding Required:** `$13,000`
* **Completion Date:** `August 31, 2026`

### Milestone 4: Mainnet Deployment, Benchmarking & Documentation

* **Functionality:** Comprehensive security auditing, performance benchmarking, public testnet launch, production documentation, and an end-to-end reference dApp.
* **Team Size & Roles:** 2 Engineers (Igor Holt and Andrew Kovach).
* **Funding Required:** `$10,000`
* **Completion Date:** `September 30, 2026`

## Total Budget Requested

| Milestone # | Description | Deliverables | Completion Date | Funding |
|===|===|===|===|===|
| Milestone 1 | Core Rust Engine & Wasm Compilation | `filevect-core` library, HNSW indexing, quantization, unit test suite | May 31, 2026 | `$12,000` |
| Milestone 2 | FVM Integration & Smart Contracts | Solidity/Rust FVM contracts, verification logic, gas optimization | July 15, 2026 | `$15,000` |
| Milestone 3 | Gateway Node & TypeScript SDK | `filevect-node` service, `@filevect/sdk`, CLI tooling | August 31, 2026 | `$13,000` |
| Milestone 4 | Benchmarking, Audit & Documentation | Testnet deployment, benchmark report, reference dApp, developer docs | September 30, 2026 | `$10,000` |
| **Total** | | | | **$50,000** |

## Maintenance and Upgrade Plans

Following successful grant completion, long-term maintenance will be sustained through a dual approach: open-source community contributions governed by a transparent roadmap, and enterprise support/managed gateway services for production teams requiring enterprise-grade SLAs. We commit to regular security patches, dependency updates, and continuous integration improvements aligned with future FVM upgrades.
